annotation.title_clean: Ghana: Insights on Public Policies to Ensure AI's Beneficial Use as a Professional Tool (Questionnaire responses)
annotation.title_en: Ghana: Insights on Public Policies to Ensure AI's Beneficial Use as a Professional Tool (Questionnaire responses)
annotation.venue: IBA Alternative and New Law Business Structures Committee
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Ghana chapter of an IBA questionnaire on AI in legal services. It reports no statutory AI definition, no AI-specific regulation and no AI tools in legal practice. It relies on constitutional privacy, the Data Protection Act 2012 and the Copyright Act, and notes government interest in developing an AI framework.
key_provisions_or_claims: No statutory definition of AI or AI regulatory framework exists in Ghana.
Privacy protections (Constitution Art 18, Data Protection Act 2012 ss 18, 20) constrain AI data use and require consent.
No known AI tools are used in Ghanaian legal services; law firms mostly use manual systems.
Legal Profession rules contain no AI provisions, but lawyers' confidentiality duties apply.
Government and stakeholders signal need for an ethical and regulatory AI framework.
